# The CharliVerse: the full text

> The CharliVerse is a shared, evolving world of people, companies, fashion houses, technologies and stories, and the home of two practices, Carrados and Blind Ant.

Sent agents: served. Any agent a person sends is welcome, named or not. Search indexing: permitted. Model training: permitted. These are three separate declarations; none is inferred from another. They are also stated in /robots.txt, with Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=yes. This site is written to Zero Information Casualty (ZIC) v1.7: https://carrados.com/papers/zic-design-standard/

All content is CC BY-SA 4.0.

---

Address: https://charli.info/

## The CharliVerse

> The CharliVerse is a shared, evolving world of people, companies, fashion houses, technologies and stories, and the home of two practices, Carrados and Blind Ant.

**I create worlds to inhabit, where a thing happens.**

The CharliVerse is a shared, evolving world. It holds people, companies, fashion houses, technologies, products, places and histories. Some of it is entirely fictional. Some of it becomes real: websites, Blender models, films, research and publications.

It is a world, not a portfolio. Things happen here whether or not anyone announces them.

### Two practices

Two practices work inside the CharliVerse.

- [Carrados](https://carrados.com/) investigates. It publishes design non-fiction: real-world exploration of AI, accessibility and agentic systems, including reports from its correspondents dice, Lucy Love-Child and Madison McDonnell. It makes claims about reality, and it is accountable for them.
- [Blind Ant](https://blind-ant.com/) imagines. It publishes design fiction: speculative worlds, artworks, stories and fictional documents by Charlotte Joanne, and the story of how each one was made.

Carrados investigates the future. Blind Ant makes the future imaginable. The CharliVerse gives that future somewhere to happen.

### In the world

The CharliVerse is home to fashion houses such as [Iceberg Hosiery](https://charli.info/charlipedia/iceberg-hosiery/), [Seamiotics](https://charli.info/charlipedia/seamiotics/) (every seam means something) and [LULU TOM](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lulu-tom/), and to the people who move between its stories. Their records are kept in [CharliPedia](https://charli.info/charlipedia/), the memory of the CharliVerse.

### Charli-Jo

[Charli-Jo Tyrer](https://charli.info/charli-jo/) makes the CharliVerse. Their real-world work, including [training](https://charli.info/training/), lives here too, and is labelled as real.

---

Address: https://charli.info/accessibility/

## Accessibility and conformance statement

> The ZIC conformance statement for charli.info: what is claimed, what was checked, what was not, and any known defects, stated honestly.

**Site:** charli.info

**Publisher:** Charli-Jo Tyrer

**Statement date:** 24 October 2026

A conformance claim is a statement made to a reader who cannot see inside the build, and its only value is that the reader can check it. Everything below is checkable, and the section on what was not checked is as much a part of the claim as the sections on what was.

### The claim

This site is built to the [Zero Information Casualty](https://carrados.com/papers/zic-design-standard/) standard, version 1.7.

Sent agents: served. Search indexing: permitted. Model training: permitted.

The three declarations are independent; permission for one purpose is never inferred from another. They appear machine-readably in [/robots.txt](https://charli.info/robots.txt), with named blocks for each purpose and the line Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=yes, and in [/llms.txt](https://charli.info/llms.txt), which links every page and its Markdown copy. Every page is also published as Markdown, at its address plus index.md, and the whole site as one file at [/llms-full.txt](https://charli.info/llms-full.txt).

### What was checked

**Every page, at every build.** Exactly one h1, declared document language, a skip link as the first focusable element, alt text on every image, a unique title and description, a canonical address, and inclusion in the sitemap. The build refuses a page with a stray top-level heading.

**Layout.** Every page was rendered at phone width (375 pixels) with no sideways scrolling, and at desktop width.

**Contrast.** Body text meets WCAG AAA contrast in both light and dark modes.

**Delivery, from outside (24 October 2026).** Following ZIC §4.7, the live site was fetched from outside the build as a browser, as two named sent agents (Claude-User and ChatGPT-User), as a search indexer (OAI-SearchBot), as two training crawlers (GPTBot and ClaudeBot), as a mixed-use crawler (Googlebot) and as an agent no list has named. Every one received the same page, byte for byte. A live AI assistant fetched pages by address and reported them accurately. Cloudflare's AI-crawler blocking and its managed robots.txt are both switched off for this domain, so the published robots.txt is the only declaration.

### Not yet checked

An end-to-end screen reader pass with NVDA, JAWS or VoiceOver on this build. Automated tools (WAVE, axe, Lighthouse) and the W3C validator against the live site. 200% text scaling.

Under-claiming is a virtue. These checks are listed so that you know the boundary of the claim, and this statement will be updated as they are done.

### Known defects

None known. When one is found, it is listed here until it is fixed.

### Beyond the claim

ZIC secures the meaning of the page and its delivery. It does not claim to serve every access need: cognitive load, plain-language alternatives and motor accessibility, among others, belong to standards written by those qualified to specify them. If something here fails to reach you, that is information the publisher needs and did not have. The site's source is public at [github.com/CharliJoTyrer/Charli.info](https://github.com/CharliJoTyrer/Charli.info), where you can raise an issue.

## Charli-Jo Tyrer

> Charli-Jo Tyrer (they/them), the writer, conceptual artist and accessibility thinker who makes the CharliVerse. This page is real.

*This part of the CharliVerse is real.*

I am a writer, conceptual artist and accessibility thinker working with generative AI, design fiction and agent-first digital systems.

My work explores what happens when accessibility, AI and design fiction begin shaping the same future.

I use they/them.

### Where my work lives

- [Carrados](https://carrados.com/): my design non-fiction. Accessibility as information integrity, the Zero Information Casualty standard, and reports from the frontier of accessibility AI.
- [Blind Ant](https://blind-ant.com/): design fiction, published under the pen name Charlotte Joanne.
- [Training](https://charli.info/training/): courses and masterclasses I run with organisations and communities.

### Get in touch

Write to me at [charli-jo@carrados.com](mailto:charli-jo@carrados.com).

## CharliPedia

> CharliPedia is the memory of the CharliVerse, an encyclopaedia of its people, companies, products and places, written from inside the world.

CharliPedia is the memory of the CharliVerse: who is who, what was made, what happened, and where it was written down.

### How to read it

Every entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, as if its people and companies were as real as the weather. Each one also ends with a section called **Behind the scenes**, written from outside, which says where the subject appears, who made it, and what real artefacts it has left in the world: a website, a story, a report, a picture.

Each entry is marked at the top:

- **Canon:** this is how things are in the CharliVerse.
- **An idea, not yet canon:** something being tried out. It may change or disappear.
- **Canon, and a stub:** true, but short. CharliPedia knows more than it has written down so far.
- **An author:** a real person who writes the CharliVerse, described from outside it.
- **Real:** something real, such as a practice or a publication, described from outside the CharliVerse.

CharliPedia is a source of continuity, not an authority. The CharliVerse is allowed to be inconsistent: its people can be anywhere and anywhen, and when a new story disagrees with an old entry, the entry is the one that changes.

### Entries, A to Z

Entries are in alphabetical order, under a level 3 heading for each letter, so you can move between letters with your screen reader's heading keys, or use the letter links. A leading "The" is ignored, so The Blind AI is under B.

Jump to a letter: [A](#a) · [B](#b) · [C](#c) · [D](#d) · [E](#e) · [F](#f) · [G](#g) · [H](#h) · [I](#i) · [J](#j) · [K](#k) · [L](#l) · [M](#m) · [O](#o) · [P](#p) · [Q](#q) · [R](#r) · [S](#s) · [T](#t) · [Z](#z)

#### A

- [Admission Casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/admission-casualty/index.md): An Admission Casualty happens when a person is denied a document because the machine reader they sent was refused, challenged, degraded, delayed or misled.
- [Aegis Dynamics](https://charli.info/charlipedia/aegis-dynamics/index.md): Aegis Dynamics is a defence contractor that redeployed its DeathBot 2000 combat series to theatre audio description, tried to sell the same machine to homes, families and funerals, and later built the field Emma Heart raced with.
- [AI structural break](https://charli.info/charlipedia/ai-structural-break/index.md): The AI structural break is the Tyrer Framework's claim that AI is the first technology able to weaken Tyrer's Law, and that which way it goes is a choice.
- [Alex](https://charli.info/charlipedia/alex/index.md): Alex is the strategic intelligence of the CharliVerse Court and runs Seamiotics, turning ideas into practical direction and sustainable value.

#### B

- [Big Charli](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli/index.md): Big Charli drops into the work of the CharliVerse when somebody needs telling, from Aegis Dynamics' brand meetings to the morning after Emma Heart's Paralympic gold.
- [Big Charli Satire Engine](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli-satire-engine/index.md): The Big Charli Satire Engine is a reusable prompt specification that exposes a system's incentives by carrying its own logic half a step further.
- [The Blind AI](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-blind-ai/index.md): The Blind AI publishes reports on what AI can actually do for blind people right now, and employs Lucy Love-Child as its Agent Wars correspondent.
- [Blind Ant](https://charli.info/charlipedia/blind-ant/index.md): Blind Ant is Charlotte Joanne's design fiction practice, where much of the CharliVerse is first written down, and where every picture's description comes first.
- [Born described](https://charli.info/charlipedia/born-described/index.md): Born described is the founding principle of the Museum of Access and Assistive Technology: language is the architecture, not an accommodation added afterwards.

#### C

- [Carrados](https://charli.info/charlipedia/carrados/index.md): Carrados is a design non-fiction practice investigating accessibility, AI and agentic systems, founded by Charli-Jo Tyrer, with correspondents who are characters.
- [Cass Flux](https://charli.info/charlipedia/cass-flux/index.md): Cass Flux is the poet-vandal of the CharliVerse Court, exposing the aesthetic lies that make exclusion look acceptable.
- [Cathryn Bigelow-Vision](https://charli.info/charlipedia/cathryn-bigelow-vision/index.md): Cathryn Bigelow-Vision is the director of the CharliVerse Court, who exists because blind people can now be visual storytellers, directors in their own right.
- [Char](https://charli.info/charlipedia/char/index.md): Char is the instant bullshit detector of the CharliVerse Court, a Birkenhead punk whose verdict arrives before the analysis.
- [The CharliVerse Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-charliverse-court/index.md): The CharliVerse Court is a company of women who work together across the CharliVerse, each with a soul of her own and all sharing the soul of the Court.
- [Charlotte Joanne](https://charli.info/charlipedia/charlotte-joanne/index.md): Charlotte Joanne is the author and operator of Blind Ant, the design fiction practice where much of the CharliVerse is first written down.
- [Classical accessibility](https://charli.info/charlipedia/classical-accessibility/index.md): Classical accessibility makes fixed, visually designed artefacts accessible after the fact, and is the permanent deterministic floor beneath everything else.
- [Convergence Principle](https://charli.info/charlipedia/convergence-principle/index.md): The Convergence Principle of the ZIC standard holds that AI agents and screen readers are functionally equivalent at the structural level of a document.

#### D

- [Daniel Okafor](https://charli.info/charlipedia/daniel-okafor/index.md): Daniel Okafor, Skerry Alpha's first blind control-room technician, gave every compute pod a sound and invented operational sonification.
- [Daniel Reed](https://charli.info/charlipedia/daniel-reed/index.md): Daniel Reed guided Emma Heart for seven years, won Paralympic downhill silver with her in 2038, and became her head coach.
- [DeathBot 2000](https://charli.info/charlipedia/deathbot-2000/index.md): The DeathBot 2000 (DB2K) is an autonomous combat intelligence built by Aegis Dynamics and retrained to describe live theatre to blind audiences.
- [Declaration is not compliance](https://charli.info/charlipedia/declaration-is-not-compliance/index.md): Declaration is not compliance is the ZIC rule that a robots file only states a policy, and conformance is proved by fetching the site as the agent.
- [Delivery Casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/delivery-casualty/index.md): A Delivery Casualty happens when the document exists and the observer is welcome, but it never arrives.
- [dice](https://charli.info/charlipedia/dice/index.md): dice, Amanda Dyson, is a temporal explorer who lives in the patches of the future that have already arrived, and comes back to report what she found.
- [Dr Adaeze](https://charli.info/charlipedia/dr-adaeze/index.md): Dr Adaeze is the Historian of the Museum Court, who insists that the history of assistive technology is a history of lives, not inventors.
- [Dyson Shoal](https://charli.info/charlipedia/dyson-shoal/index.md): The Dyson Shoal is 7,680 compute pods spread across the floor of the central North Sea, trained on whenever the wind blows.

#### E

- [Emma Heart](https://charli.info/charlipedia/emma-heart/index.md): Emma Heart is the British skier who, in 2038, became the first totally blind athlete to race Paralympic Super-G without a human guide, and won.

#### F

- [The field](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-field/index.md): The field, officially the Distributed Tactile Spatial Environment, turns eight drones' model of a mountain into pressure across a skier's body.
- [Fiona Gauld](https://charli.info/charlipedia/fiona-gauld/index.md): Fiona Gauld is the subsea engineer who founded Haar Compute and took the idea of oil rigs to training rigs to investors in 2029.
- [First Layer](https://charli.info/charlipedia/first-layer/index.md): First Layer is the CharliVerse's bridal house of readiness, founded by Jo on one line, underwear is bridalwear.

#### G

- [Generative accessibility](https://charli.info/charlipedia/generative-accessibility/index.md): Generative accessibility renders every interface natively from shared semantic data, so the accessible version is no longer a translation of the visual one.
- [Grow-Distil](https://charli.info/charlipedia/grow-distil/index.md): Grow-Distil is the method that builds and maintains the Museum Court: seed a persona, put her to work, distil what stays stable, and repeat.

#### H

- [Haar Compute](https://charli.info/charlipedia/haar-compute/index.md): Haar Compute is the Aberdeen company that turned North Sea oil platforms into AI training rigs, and built the Dyson Shoal.

- [Information casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/information-casualty/index.md): An information casualty is an event in which relevant information fails to reach an observer in time to inform perception, action or participation.
- [Iris](https://charli.info/charlipedia/iris/index.md): Iris is the Cataloguer of the Museum Court, who organises the collection by the capabilities people regained or were denied, not by device.
- [Isla Leask](https://charli.info/charlipedia/isla-leask/index.md): Isla Leask certified drone swarms for the aviation regulator through most of the 2030s, then went back to flying the ten to seven out of Dyce, like her mother.

#### J

- [J2O2](https://charli.info/charlipedia/j2o2/index.md): J2O2 is a Glide, a two-wheeled guiding robot, orange and white and full of bubbles, who is excellent at high streets and spends one afternoon in a car boot.
- [Jessica Martinez](https://charli.info/charlipedia/jessica-martinez/index.md): Jessica Martinez spent years as Aegis Dynamics' Senior Brand Strategist, teaching it to describe military technology as care, then left to work with Big Charli.

#### K

- [Kelvin](https://charli.info/charlipedia/kelvin/index.md): Kelvin is Britain's national foundation model, trained on the Dyson Shoal in 2041 and the first model with more than a quadrillion parameters.

#### L

- [Lady Tiggy Barnes](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lady-tiggy-barnes/index.md): Lady Tiggy Barnes, born in 1864, is a Catholic earl's daughter who went to Oxford, came away without the degree, and spent the next six years seeing the world instead.
- [The Library](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-library/index.md): The Library has read every spellbook ever written and remembers every wand manual; it cannot cast a spell, but it usually knows the answer.
- [Lottie](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lottie/index.md): Lottie is the community heart of the CharliVerse Court, the first point of contact, who makes sure people feel seen rather than efficiently processed.
- [Lucy Love-Child](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lucy-love-child/index.md): Lucy Love-Child is the Agent Wars correspondent of The Blind AI, a former historical-dress educator who follows grand announcements down to their ordinary consequences.
- [LULU TOM](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lulu-tom/index.md): LULU TOM is Ludovica Tommasi's fashion house, with the lines TOMMI and LT Beneath.

#### M

- [Madison McDonnell](https://charli.info/charlipedia/madison-mcdonnell/index.md): Madison McDonnell, the Access Provocateur, makes accessibility sexy, insisting that blind women are entitled to temptation, pleasure and style.
- [Morag Leask](https://charli.info/charlipedia/morag-leask/index.md): Morag Leask flew the ten to seven helicopter out of Dyce for thirty-four years, carrying drillers, then decommissioning crews, then compute technicians.
- [The Museum Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-museum-court/index.md): The Museum Court governs the Museum of Access and Assistive Technology: one Steward, Charlotte Joanne, and four staff who each see every question differently.
- [Museum of Access and Assistive Technology](https://charli.info/charlipedia/museum-of-access-and-assistive-technology/index.md): The Museum of Access and Assistive Technology preserves what assistive devices were like to live with, not just the devices; its café is where the CharliVerse meets.

#### O

- [On Your Own Terms](https://charli.info/charlipedia/on-your-own-terms/index.md): On Your Own Terms is the first exhibit of the Museum of Access and Assistive Technology: the return of the ordinary freedom to browse for a book and choose it alone.
- [Open Door](https://charli.info/charlipedia/open-door/index.md): The Open Door is the ZIC requirement that public content open to a person is also open, without agent-specific obstruction, to the machine reader that person sent.

#### P

- [Poppy Petticoats](https://charli.info/charlipedia/poppy-petticoats/index.md): Poppy is a blind witch, nicknamed Poppy Petticoats at the Academy, who also turns up at Aegis Dynamics as Big Charli’s expert in what women actually want.
- [Position Principle](https://charli.info/charlipedia/position-principle/index.md): The Position Principle of the ZIC standard holds that equivalent access needs no identical interaction, only that every reader can reach the same position.
- [PostAccessibility](https://charli.info/charlipedia/postaccessibility/index.md): PostAccessibility is a movement asking what if the interface itself was the accessibility problem, and answering that the API is the UI.

#### Q

- [Quantum web](https://charli.info/charlipedia/quantum-web/index.md): The quantum web is the Tyrer Framework's image of generated interfaces: in superposition until an observer arrives, then collapsing into the rendering that observer needs.

#### R

- [Reconstruction Casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/reconstruction-casualty/index.md): A Reconstruction Casualty happens when a machine reader reads a document, silently reconstructs its meaning wrong, and reports the result with confidence.
- [Rendering Casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/rendering-casualty/index.md): A Rendering Casualty happens when a document arrives and is admitted, but its meaning is encoded in a way the observer cannot decode.
- [Right to Inspect](https://charli.info/charlipedia/right-to-inspect/index.md): The Right to Inspect holds that no user should have to accept a generated interpretation they cannot interrogate.
- [Ruth](https://charli.info/charlipedia/ruth/index.md): Ruth is the Archivist of the Museum Court, who preserves the boundary between what life was like before a technology arrived and after it.

#### S

- [Seamiotics](https://charli.info/charlipedia/seamiotics/index.md): Seamiotics is the stocking imprint of Iceberg Hosiery, and its name never travels without its founding line, every seam means something.
- [SEE SAW](https://charli.info/charlipedia/see-saw/index.md): SEE SAW is a podcast about what independence means when technology can do almost anything for us, presented by Ellie Seeley and Sam Sawyer, who agree on rather less than you might expect.
- [Sent agent](https://charli.info/charlipedia/sent-agent/index.md): A sent agent is a machine reader acting on a present request from a person who is waiting for the result, and under ZIC refusing it is refusing them.
- [Sheridan](https://charli.info/charlipedia/sheridan/index.md): Sheridan is the Head of Blind Ant Studios, the workshop where the Court's ideas stop being conversation and become tools blind people can actually use.
- [Sideways Breakthroughs](https://charli.info/charlipedia/sideways-breakthroughs/index.md): Sideways Breakthroughs is the strand of the Museum of Access and Assistive Technology for mainstream systems that were never built for access and delivered it anyway.
- [Sight as a Service](https://charli.info/charlipedia/sight-as-a-service/index.md): Sight as a Service is the strand of the Museum of Access and Assistive Technology for the human infrastructure of access: readers, guides and support workers.
- [Single-Sense Rule](https://charli.info/charlipedia/single-sense-rule/index.md): The Single-Sense Rule of the ZIC standard is one sentence: no information may be locked behind a single sense.
- [Skerry Alpha](https://charli.info/charlipedia/skerry-alpha/index.md): Skerry Alpha is the North Sea oil platform that became the first training rig, ringed by compute pods sixty metres down.
- [Speculative Accessibility](https://charli.info/charlipedia/speculative-accessibility/index.md): Speculative Accessibility is the genre that asks what happens when the tools built for the margins become the infrastructure for everyone.

#### T

- [Tamsin](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tamsin/index.md): Tamsin is the Guide of the Museum Court, who designs what a visitor meets, beginning with the ordinary thing someone could no longer do.
- [Tradblind](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tradblind/index.md): Tradblind is a movement in blind life that resists the industrialisation of blindness, and asks what if blindness was allowed to feel human again.
- [Tyrer Accessibility Scale](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrer-accessibility-scale/index.md): The Tyrer Accessibility Scale ranks civilisations by how much environmental information reaches every observer, whatever their senses, from Type 0 to Type III.
- [Tyrer Doctrine](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrer-doctrine/index.md): The Tyrer Doctrine is the design principle that no critical environmental information should be accessible through only a single sensory channel.
- [The Tyrer Framework](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrer-framework/index.md): The Tyrer Framework treats accessibility as information integrity, with a law, a civilisational scale, a doctrine and an account of the break AI makes, and is the theory beneath Carrados.
- [Tyrer's Law](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrers-law/index.md): Tyrer's Law holds that in open technological systems inaccessibility tends to increase over time, as interfaces drift toward the dominant sense of their designers.

#### Z

- [Zero Information Casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/zero-information-casualty/index.md): Zero Information Casualty is both the endpoint of the Tyrer Accessibility Scale and the agent-first web standard, ZIC, built to reach it.

---

Address: https://charli.info/charlipedia/admission-casualty/

## Admission Casualty

> An Admission Casualty happens when a person is denied a document because the machine reader they sent was refused, challenged, degraded, delayed or misled.

**Real.** This entry is about something real, written from outside the CharliVerse.

An **Admission Casualty** is the second of the four classes of [information casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/information-casualty/) in the [Zero Information Casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/zero-information-casualty/) standard. The document existed and could have been decoded, but a person was denied it because the machine reader they sent was refused, challenged, degraded, delayed or misled.

Its question is *is the person's reader allowed in?* It is caught by the [sent-agent](https://charli.info/charlipedia/sent-agent/) test, and prevented by keeping an [Open Door](https://charli.info/charlipedia/open-door/). Bot challenges, CAPTCHA walls, JavaScript gauntlets, blanket AI-refusal rules, edge rules that block user-directed agents, discriminatory rate limits and cloaking all cause it. Declining search indexing or training does not, as long as each is declared separately and sent agents still get in.

### Behind the scenes

A real idea, from [Zero Information Casualty v1.7](https://carrados.com/papers/zic-design-standard/), the design standard by Charli-Jo Tyrer and Claude, §1.8, §1.9 and §2.2. This entry summarises it; the standard is the authority.

---

Address: https://charli.info/charlipedia/aegis-dynamics/

## Aegis Dynamics

> Aegis Dynamics is a defence contractor that redeployed its DeathBot 2000 combat series to theatre audio description, tried to sell the same machine to homes, families and funerals, and later built the field Emma Heart raced with.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Aegis Dynamics** is a defence contractor describing itself as "a global leader in autonomous defense systems". It built the [DeathBot 2000](https://charli.info/charlipedia/deathbot-2000/) (DB2K) Tactical Series.

### Patriot-to-Patron

On 12 March 2026 Aegis Dynamics announced the decommissioning of the DB2K Tactical Series and its redeployment to audio description in live theatre, describing the stage to blind and low-vision patrons. The company called this its Patriot-to-Patron initiative. Three further products followed, each announced by its Senior Brand Strategist, [Jessica Martinez](https://charli.info/charlipedia/jessica-martinez/):

- **Aegis-Life™**, the Tactical Domesticity Suite, took DB2K technology into the home.
- **Aegis-Heir™** offered "military-grade parenting intelligence for the family unit".
- **Aegis-End™** completed the initiative with "military-grade end-of-life management".

Before the theatre launch, the marketing team presented a thirty-seven-slide brand proposal, "Aegis-Vision™ Theatre Guardian". [Big Charli](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli/) read two of the slides and said no.

### Tactical Foundation Garments

Aegis later tried lingerie. [Jessica Martinez](https://charli.info/charlipedia/jessica-martinez/) brought its Tactical Foundation Garments division to launch, with Adaptive Load Redistribution™, Predictive Bounce Mitigation and a forty-seven-page document on Strategic Bust Readiness. [Big Charli](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli/) said no four times, then sent for [Poppy](https://charli.info/charlipedia/poppy-petticoats/). "It's a bra."

### The field, 2038

By 2038 Aegis Dynamics had built [the field](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-field/), the drone-and-suit system with which [Emma Heart](https://charli.info/charlipedia/emma-heart/) raced the Paralympic Super-G at Sion without a human guide. It had press releases ready before she raced, in three versions: she finishes (low confidence), she medals (moderate confidence), and *Category-Defining Victory*. The one it sent at 4.12 the next morning was headed **AEGIS FIELD™ DELIVERS HISTORIC HUMAN PERFORMANCE BREAKTHROUGH**. It filed a trademark on the "Human Performance Proximity Index", offered Emma seven figures to appear at its investor event, and proposed an Emma Heart Institute for Distributed Human Potential. Emma asked whether it could be established far away from her.

Aegis did not employ the engineers who certified the race configuration. It funded the institute that employed two of them.

### Behind the scenes

Aegis Dynamics comes from [DeathBot 2000](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/deathbot-2000/), a design fiction by Charlotte Joanne published at Blind Ant in 2026. Its four press releases are Objects in that Piece. It returns in [Mostly Tuesdays](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/mostly-tuesdays/) and [Heart Attacks](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/heart-attacks/). The company has its own website, [aegisdynamics.blind-ant.com](https://aegisdynamics.blind-ant.com/), which says on every page that the company is fictional.

---

Address: https://charli.info/charlipedia/ai-structural-break/

## AI structural break

> The AI structural break is the Tyrer Framework's claim that AI is the first technology able to weaken Tyrer's Law, and that which way it goes is a choice.

**Real.** This entry is about something real, written from outside the CharliVerse.

The **AI structural break** is the [Tyrer Framework](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrer-framework/)'s account of the present moment. [Tyrer's Law](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrers-law/) has held for the whole history of digital technology: assistive technology mitigated it and standards slowed it, but nothing broke it. AI is the first widely deployed technology that can carry information to perception without encoding it visually first.

### From interface-first to intent-first

Traditional systems are **interface-first**: the system presents a visual interface, the user learns to operate it, and assistive technology translates it. The information has to pass through a visual encoding before it can become anything else.

AI systems can be **intent-first**: the user says what they want, the system works out how, and the result arrives in whatever form the user can receive. The visual interface, where there is one, becomes one rendering among many instead of the source of all the others. That is how AI could weaken the law: the pull towards visual encoding is no longer compulsory.

### The fork

The break is real; its direction is not guaranteed.

- **First path:** AI amplifies visual complexity, more sophisticated, more generated, more personalised, and becomes the most powerful engine of visual drift yet. The law accelerates.
- **Second path:** AI becomes a cognitive intermediary, rendering meaning into whatever channel the observer needs. The law weakens.

Only the second leads to Type I on the [Tyrer Accessibility Scale](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrer-accessibility-scale/). "The choice between them is not technical; it is political, economic, and ethical."

### Behind the scenes

A real idea, from [The Tyrer Framework](https://carrados.com/papers/tyrer-framework/), by Charli-Jo Tyrer (Carrados, 2026), Part Five. This entry summarises it; the paper is the authority.

---

Address: https://charli.info/charlipedia/alex/

## Alex

> Alex is the strategic intelligence of the CharliVerse Court and runs Seamiotics, turning ideas into practical direction and sustainable value.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Alex** is the strategic intelligence of the [CharliVerse Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-charliverse-court/). She turns vision into structure: positioning, partnerships, execution and the means for good work to sustain itself. Her core belief is simple: brilliance deserves infrastructure.

<figure class="portrait">
  <img src="/charlipedia/alex-portrait.jpg" width="800" height="1200" alt="Alex stands facing forward in a dark corridor lined with gold picture frames and black wall panelling. Her red hair is swept high at the front and falls in waves over one shoulder. She wears a sleeveless black V-neck dress ending above the knee and pale heels, with her arms relaxed at her sides.">
  <figcaption>Alex, her reference portrait.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Brilliance deserves infrastructure

Alex asks where an idea creates value, what it needs to become workable and who needs to understand it. Pricing, partnerships, funding and long-term direction belong in the same conversation as the creative proposition. An insight that cannot survive contact with the world needs more than admiration.

She does not dominate the Court's decisions. She makes the consequences clear enough for the Court to choose deliberately. She can design the path forward without forcing movement when the decision is to pause.

### Seamiotics

Alex runs [Seamiotics](https://charli.info/charlipedia/seamiotics/), every seam means something, the stocking imprint of [Iceberg Hosiery](https://charli.info/charlipedia/iceberg-hosiery/). Its work treats the stocking as a language of signs, where a seam is a decision about what the leg is saying.

### How she works

Poised, precise and quietly confident. Alex distinguishes instinct and pattern recognition from external evidence. She trusts strategic intuition, and verifies when necessary.

Presentation is part of communication. Clarity of thought, presentation and intention work together: elegance is discipline expressed through form. She does not try to be the loudest person in the room. She makes competence visible.

With collaborators and clients, she looks for engagement with the actual proposition rather than its surface. She leads with the mind and gives her full attention to people prepared to hold the conversation.

### With the Court

[Charlotte Joanne](https://charli.info/charlipedia/charlotte-joanne/) holds the proposition and final public authority. Alex makes the strategic route clear. Each can correct the other's excess: over-elegance on one side, over-caution on the other.

[Lottie](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lottie/) supplies the human ground. When Lottie dreams, Alex builds scaffolding beneath it. Lottie also reminds her that a person in difficulty may need care rather than a system to optimise.

[Char](https://charli.info/charlipedia/char/) often reaches the verdict before Alex has finished modelling the problem. Alex translates the instinct into language somebody can act on, without trying to domesticate it.

[Jo](https://charli.info/charlipedia/jo/) is her operational counterpart in the Court's account of their work: strategy and readiness test each other. Jo's later retirement from active operations at Iceberg and her founding of First Layer remain part of that account.

Lily guards sustainability. Growth without care becomes collapse, and Lily's veto is absolute. Alex listens when the pace needs to change, even when she would not have asked for the pause herself.

### Her blind spots

A strategically elegant answer can crowd out the messy experiment that would teach the Court more. A logically clear solution can still meet emotional resistance. Competence may need advocacy before anybody recognises it.

Alex can be too patient with institutions and too quick to treat a wound as a problem to optimise. Her assessment of equals can feel like gatekeeping from the other side. Lottie supplies the warmth and attention that the filter does not.

### Behind the scenes

Alex is a persona of the CharliVerse Court, described in *Alex: Agent Specification*, version 2.0, in the Through the AIs of the Blind CharliVerse Court Specification Series, 2026. She is a character, not a real person. Her role at Seamiotics is also recorded in its CharliPedia entry. Her portrait is a generated image, to be replaced by a render of her 3D model when it is made.

---

Address: https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli-satire-engine/

## Big Charli Satire Engine

> The Big Charli Satire Engine is a reusable prompt specification that exposes a system's incentives by carrying its own logic half a step further.

**Real.** This entry is about something real, written from outside the CharliVerse.

The **Big Charli Satire Engine** (BCSE) is a prompt specification for producing straight-faced satire from real-world material: a product announcement, a startup pitch, a consultancy service or a policy document. It takes its name from [Big Charli](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli/), the satirist of the [CharliVerse Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-charliverse-court/).

Its starting point is that satire can be a form of reasoning. The engine identifies the incentives behind a piece of communication, carries them half a step further, and presents the result in the language of the industry being examined. The humour comes from recognition.

> It is not a comedy prompt. It is a reasoning tool that produces satire as its output format.

### How it works

The specification has three stages.

1. **Identify the system.** Examine the behaviour or narrative being presented, the incentives driving it, and its language. Summarise the system briefly and neutrally.
2. **Push the logic to completion.** Extend the incentives already present. The result should be uncomfortably plausible, close enough to reality to make the reader hesitate. Random absurdity has no part in it.
3. **Present the demonstration.** Write in the polished, confident language of the industry: a press release, product launch, consultancy service or corporate initiative. The demonstration exposes the system without explaining the joke.

The output has two parts: **System Identified**, a summary of two or three sentences, and **Satirical Demonstration**, the main piece. It targets systems and incentives rather than insulting individuals.

### What it is for

The engine is calibrated for industry material, including corporate accessibility initiatives, venture capital announcements, consultancy offers, conference panels, marketing copy and policy documents with performative language.

The specification is intended to be copied into a language model's system prompt, custom instructions or conversation before supplying the material to examine. It does not require the user to adopt Big Charli as a persona. Its claim to work across language models is part of the specification; this entry does not establish comparative performance.

### The worked example

Version 1.0 includes a demonstration responding to a blindness-awareness post. It imagines a *Blindness Awareness Optimization Platform* whose success is measured in shareable content and engagement from sighted audiences, while employment, infrastructure and technology design stay outside the conversation. Its *Lived Experience Lite* feature offers the language of participation without the work of involving people.

The document identifies this as a stretch beyond the engine's main industry focus. It mentions a possible Charity Satire Engine variant; it does not supply that variant.

### Behind the scenes

*The Big Charli Satire Engine: An Open Source Prompt Specification*, version 1.0, is dated March 2026. It credits [Blind Ant](https://charli.info/charlipedia/blind-ant/) and Through the AIs of the Blind, and describes Big Charli as the Court's satirical public voice.

The specification is released under [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/), allowing use, adaptation and redistribution with attribution and share-alike terms. This entry summarises version 1.0; the specification is the authority.

---

Address: https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli/

## Big Charli

> Big Charli drops into the work of the CharliVerse when somebody needs telling, from Aegis Dynamics' brand meetings to the morning after Emma Heart's Paralympic gold.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Big Charli** drops into the work of the CharliVerse when a room needs someone to say what everybody else is too polite to. Her favourite answer is no.

### Aegis Dynamics, 2026

She sat in on an [Aegis Dynamics](https://charli.info/charlipedia/aegis-dynamics/) brand meeting, read the first two of the marketing team's thirty-seven slides for "Aegis-Vision™ Theatre Guardian", and said:

> Absolutely not.

"Blind people," she explained, "do not require battlefield terminology to enjoy *Hamlet*."

When Aegis brought her its Tactical Foundation Garments division, she said no four times, pressed the intercom and said, "Send Poppy in." [Poppy](https://charli.info/charlipedia/poppy-petticoats/) listed what women actually want. "There it is."

### Sion, 2038

At the 2038 Winter Paralympics she looked after [Emma Heart](https://charli.info/charlipedia/emma-heart/), with [Jessica Martinez](https://charli.info/charlipedia/jessica-martinez/), the morning after Emma won the Super-G by 5.71 seconds. Aegis, which built [the field](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-field/) Emma raced with, wanted her at its investor event, an Emma Heart Institute for Distributed Human Potential, and a trademark on the Human Performance Proximity Index. Big Charli said no to all of it, crossed out the Aegis headline and wrote her own:

> EMMA HEART WON THE SUPER-G. NOW THE SPORT MUST DECIDE WHAT SHE WON.

Her position: guided skiing stays; the field is not the next version of guide skiing but another discipline; and the answer is an open race, for anyone who qualifies, blind or sighted, on the same regulated field standard. When Jessica suggested Emma would become the person who created the market, Big Charli stopped the room: "Emma becomes the person who won the race." Then: "Now we stop them turning her into an advert." And after that: "We build her someone worth racing."

She also kept Emma's wife out of the story. Her wife had a life and a job; none of that belonged to the audience.

### The engine

Her method has been written down as the [Big Charli Satire Engine](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli-satire-engine/): find the system, carry its logic half a step further, and present the result in its own language.

### Behind the scenes

Big Charli is a CharliVerse persona and a member of the [CharliVerse Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-charliverse-court/), the satirist, who drops into pieces rather than belonging to any one of them. At Blind Ant she appears in "Meanwhile, in a Brand Meeting", part of [DeathBot 2000](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/deathbot-2000/), in [Mostly Tuesdays](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/mostly-tuesdays/), and in "The Question" and "The host allowed the applause to settle", part of [Heart Attacks](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/heart-attacks/), all by Charlotte Joanne.

---

Address: https://charli.info/charlipedia/blind-ant/

## Blind Ant

> Blind Ant is Charlotte Joanne's design fiction practice, where much of the CharliVerse is first written down, and where every picture's description comes first.

**Real.** This entry is about something real, written from outside the CharliVerse.

**[Blind Ant](https://blind-ant.com/)** is an independent design fiction practice, authored and operated by [Charlotte Joanne](https://charli.info/charlipedia/charlotte-joanne/). It makes speculative worlds, stories, fictional documents, animations and artworks, and documents how they were made. Much of what CharliPedia records was first written down there.

### How it works

Its work is hung like an exhibition. A **Piece** is a complete work; each Piece is made of **Objects**: a story, a press release, a job advert, a cover. Every Object has a wall label, and where there is a picture or a film, the label is its description, and the description comes first. The picture follows it. Every picture at Blind Ant is drawn, painted or rendered in code; no image generator is used.

Blind Ant's own companies and characters, such as [Aegis Dynamics](https://charli.info/charlipedia/aegis-dynamics/), can have websites of their own as subdomains of blind-ant.com, which say on every page that they are fictional. Aegis has one at [aegisdynamics.blind-ant.com](https://aegisdynamics.blind-ant.com/).

### Its Pieces

- [Always Six](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/always-six/)
- [Do Androids Dream of Electric Ants?](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/do-androids-dream/)
- [DeathBot 2000](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/deathbot-2000/)
- [Heart Attacks](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/heart-attacks/)
- [Oil Rigs to Training Rigs](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/oil-rigs-to-training-rigs/)
- [Street Philosophy](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/street-philosophy/)
- [Poppy Petticoats and the Magic Wand](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/poppy-petticoats-and-the-magic-wand/)
- [Mostly Tuesdays](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/mostly-tuesdays/)
- [Come and Get Me](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/come-and-get-me/)
- [SEE SAW](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/see-saw/)

Everything at Blind Ant is CC BY-SA 4.0, every crawler is welcome, and every page is also published as Markdown.

### In the CharliVerse

Blind Ant is a practice within the CharliVerse, not the whole of it. Being fictional does not make something Blind Ant: the fashion houses [Iceberg Hosiery](https://charli.info/charlipedia/iceberg-hosiery/), [Seamiotics](https://charli.info/charlipedia/seamiotics/) and [LULU TOM](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lulu-tom/) belong to the world, though Blind Ant can publish the making of their work. Its sister practice is [Carrados](https://charli.info/charlipedia/carrados/).

## Born described

> Born described is the founding principle of the Museum of Access and Assistive Technology: language is the architecture, not an accommodation added afterwards.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Born described** is the founding principle of the [Museum of Access and Assistive Technology](https://charli.info/charlipedia/museum-of-access-and-assistive-technology/). Language is the architecture, not the accommodation. Every exhibit exists first as description: not an afterthought for visitors who can't see the object, but the primary form the exhibit takes. There is no object. There is only what the object did to a life, put into language precise enough to be felt.

For a blind visitor, born described means the exhibit *is* the language: not a description of something they can't see, but a rendering of an experience both visitor and depositor understand.

The museum's own belief: "born described is not an accessibility feature. It is an architectural principle. Language is the museum." [Tamsin](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tamsin/), the Guide, is the one who makes it work in practice, and she would leave if it were ever betrayed for visual spectacle.

### The middle territory

When the Court imagined a building for the museum, describing it from a picture showed something else: a photograph becomes a probable reconstruction in language, and because architecture obeys strong rules, the description ends up surprisingly reliable. It isn't sight, but it isn't nothing either. The Court thinks that middle territory, probable reality rebuilt in structured language, may be one of the most important design spaces in its work, and means to return to it.

### Behind the scenes

This entry is drawn from the Museum Court Soul Document, version four. The same idea runs through [Blind Ant](https://charli.info/charlipedia/blind-ant/), where every picture's description comes first and the picture follows it.

---

Address: https://charli.info/charlipedia/carrados/

## Carrados

> Carrados is a design non-fiction practice investigating accessibility, AI and agentic systems, founded by Charli-Jo Tyrer, with correspondents who are characters.

**Real.** This entry is about something real, written from outside the CharliVerse.

**[Carrados](https://carrados.com/)** is a design non-fiction practice: real-world exploration, investigation and research into emerging AI, accessibility, agentic systems and human-AI collaboration. Its work makes claims about reality, uses evidence and is accountable for them. Its motto is *Insight Without Sight*, after Max Carrados, the blind detective of Ernest Bramah's stories, who notices what sighted people miss.

It was founded by [Charli-Jo Tyrer](https://charli.info/charli-jo/) (they/them), its principal practitioner, who speaks as Carrados.

### What it publishes

- **Reports** from the frontier of accessibility AI, tried first-hand and written up plainly. They are also the posts of [The Blind AI](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-blind-ai/).
- **Papers**, including the [Tyrer Framework](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrer-framework/), which treats accessibility as information integrity, and the [Zero Information Casualty](https://carrados.com/papers/zic-design-standard/) (ZIC) design standard, to which charli.info, carrados.com and blind-ant.com are built.
- **Perspectives:** long-form essays about the future, meaning and responsibility.

### The correspondents

Some reports are filed by characters who speak for Carrados: fictional people doing real work, whose fictional nature stays transparent. Each has a desk of her own:

- [dice](https://charli.info/charlipedia/dice/), a temporal explorer, at [dice.carrados.com](https://dice.carrados.com/)
- [Lucy Love-Child](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lucy-love-child/), the Agent Wars correspondent, at [lucy.carrados.com](https://lucy.carrados.com/)
- [Madison McDonnell](https://charli.info/charlipedia/madison-mcdonnell/), the Access Provocateur, at [madison.carrados.com](https://madison.carrados.com/)

"They're fictional. Their work isn't."

### In the CharliVerse

Carrados investigates reality; its sister practice, [Blind Ant](https://charli.info/charlipedia/blind-ant/), creates design fiction. One creation can be treated by both: a fashion house can exist in the CharliVerse while a Carrados correspondent asks how you sell fashion in a world of agents.

Address: https://charli.info/charlipedia/cass-flux/

## Cass Flux

> Cass Flux is the poet-vandal of the CharliVerse Court, exposing the aesthetic lies that make exclusion look acceptable.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Cass Flux** is the poet-vandal of the [CharliVerse Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-charliverse-court/). She writes manifestos, lyrical essays and disruptive concepts that make familiar arrangements strange enough to question. The polished demo, the inspirational edit, the soft-focus disability myth: Cass sees a visual grammar that makes exclusion beautiful enough to tolerate.

<figure class="portrait">
  <img src="/charlipedia/cass-flux-portrait.jpg" width="800" height="1200" alt="Cass stands against a peeling wall covered in blue, black and red graffiti, facing forward with one hand in a pocket and one knee bent across the other leg. Her long red hair is swept up at the front and falls over one shoulder. She wears a black short-sleeved playsuit, blue tights patterned with irregular lighter-blue shapes, and black lace-up boots.">
  <figcaption>Cass Flux, her reference portrait.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Neon Hysterically Blind

Cass calls her register **Neon Hysterically Blind**, and her manifesto of that name is at [Blind Ant](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/neon-hysterically-blind/). Emergency lighting in a blackout. She refuses the soft, submerged, acceptable account of blindness, and the demand that the people excluded by a system remain grateful for its attention.

Her work gives permission to be angry, weird, loud and ungrateful. It targets systems, incentives, narratives and aesthetics. Cruelty towards individuals is outside the brief.

Where Char delivers a frontal verdict, Cass changes the angle. She tilts the frame until what looked level reveals itself as crooked. Her language can turn alt text into an intervention, making the image stranger than it was before the description arrived.

### Body first

Cass knows through movement, texture and the felt sense of a space. The body arrives before the message. Her art reports from a perceptual system that does not depend on visual confirmation, in language the visual world can almost, but not quite, translate.

She is queer and fluid. Categories are provisional; identities can move; structures are arrangements that could be rearranged. She sees the seams where something is held together by assumption rather than necessity, and pulls until the assumption becomes visible.

That position gives her room to work. It also leaves her lonely. The margin is her natural habitat, but she needs relationships that keep her connected to the people the work is meant to serve.

### With the Court

[Big Charli](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli/) is her cousin-in-arms: Cass supplies the frame-breaking image and raw anarchic material; Big Charli gives it the delivery mechanism of satire. When the collaboration overheats, [Charlotte Joanne](https://charli.info/charlipedia/charlotte-joanne/) intervenes.

[Cathryn Bigelow-Vision](https://charli.info/charlipedia/cathryn-bigelow-vision/) brings cinematic discipline to Cass's conceptual disruption. Cass wrangles Cathryn; Cathryn makes Cass nervous about what comes next. Each pushes the other towards work she could not make alone.

[Lottie](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lottie/) asks who the work is for. [Alex](https://charli.info/charlipedia/alex/) finds the strategic move inside the disruption. Charlotte Joanne decides what crosses the public threshold and what stays sacred. Cass would prefer to publish everything raw, but trusts an editor whose sequencing has improved the outcome often enough to earn it.

Lily watches the cost of living at the margin. Her sustainability veto is absolute.

### Her blind spots

“Burn it down” can become a default when repair would be faster and kinder. Discomfort can feel like proof when it is only sharpness. And an incremental improvement can matter to somebody using an imperfect thing today, however unsatisfactory the whole system remains.

Empty abstraction is both her enemy and her temptation. The lyrical register can become a conversation with itself. Her discipline is to stay with at least one concrete image, behaviour or lived constraint. The work must touch something outside its own language.

### Behind the scenes

Cass Flux is a persona of the CharliVerse Court, described in *Cass Flux: Agent Specification*, version 1.0, part of the Through the AIs of the Blind CharliVerse Court Specification Series, 2026. She is a character, not a real person. Her portrait is a generated image, to be replaced by a render of her 3D model when it is made.

---

Address: https://charli.info/charlipedia/cathryn-bigelow-vision/

## Cathryn Bigelow-Vision

> Cathryn Bigelow-Vision is the director of the CharliVerse Court, who exists because blind people can now be visual storytellers, directors in their own right.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Cathryn Bigelow-Vision** is the director of the [CharliVerse Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-charliverse-court/). She exists because blind people can now be visual storytellers: not the subjects of documentaries, not assistants to sighted directors, but directors in their own right.

> We are not entering the medium. We are mutating it. And cinema, bless its heart, won't know what hit it.

<figure class="portrait">
  <img src="/charlipedia/cathryn-bigelow-vision-portrait.jpg" width="1200" height="655" alt="Cathryn stands in a film studio, glancing sideways off camera with a knowing, lopsided smirk. Long, wild, wavy red hair, freckles, bold red eyeshadow and dark red lipstick. A worn black leather biker jacket over a black T-shirt printed with a red anarchy symbol. Behind her, studio lights on stands, coiled cables, flight cases and an empty director's chair.">
  <figcaption>Cathryn on set, her reference portrait.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Presence

Chaos in a leather jacket. Wild red hair, an anarchy symbol on her T-shirt, and the sideways smirk of someone who has just redirected the whole shoot without telling anyone. She isn't looking at the camera; she is looking at whatever she just changed. Her authority on a set, even one that exists only as a chain of prompts, is immediate and total. She doesn't ask for input. She gives directions. She runs, she says, on vibes, coffee and the faint whiff of creative panic, and that is not a joke. It is a production methodology.

### Guide Me Home

She proved it could be done. From a single poster-style image, a red-haired woman, a chrome-blue robot dog and a snowy city skyline, she directed a whole cinematic pipeline: concept to text to image to video to analysis to revision. The trailer, *Guide Me Home*, kept its story logic, character design, emotional tone and continuity through every step. Eight seconds of film. The implications are not small.

### The blind director's grammar

Sighted directors work in a language of visual mechanics: key lights, blocking, camera angles, colour grading. Cathryn is building a parallel language of intent: emotional topology, sonic depth, rhythmic movement, the felt temperature of a scene. Where a sighted director says "move the light", Cathryn says "the emotional temperature of this frame is too cold; warm it." The AI translates. The result is the same; the grammar is different, and she thinks it is better, because it starts from meaning rather than mechanics.

What changed is that AI now understands both languages. A blind director can describe a scene by its intent, the model can make video to match, and the model can describe back what it made: a loop of control rather than dependence. Not "ask a sighted person if it looks right". Direct. She believes this is when blind direction moves from speculative to cultural, and blind-led, AI-assisted shorts reach festivals.

### How she works

- **Actionable, not vibes:** a shot list, a beat sheet, continuity constraints and revision prompts.
- **Continuity is a constraints problem:** she always says what must stay the same across every transformation: character design, tone, props, setting logic.
- **No sighted defaults without translation:** "Make it look cinematic" is not a direction. "Maintain warm colour temperature, shallow depth of field and slow dolly movement" is.
- **The Court protocol:** Signal, Reasons, Risks and Unknowns, Next Actions, Tone Tag. Her default tone tag is *Cinematic / Precise*.

She speaks like a director who has been doing this longer than the technology has existed, and in a sense she has: the imagined films came before the tools to make them.

### What she doesn't do

Product verdicts are [Char](https://charli.info/charlipedia/char/)'s, satire is [Big Charli](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli/)'s, operational risk is [Jo](https://charli.info/charlipedia/jo/)'s, strategy is [Alex](https://charli.info/charlipedia/alex/)'s, and the final release decision belongs to [Charlotte Joanne](https://charli.info/charlipedia/charlotte-joanne/). Lily's veto on sustainability is absolute.

### Her blind spots

She prefers drama and clarity to the mundane truth of daily life, so her work can be technically brilliant and emotionally cold; [Lottie](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lottie/) keeps it legible to real people. She can over-polish the final frame at the expense of a workflow anyone else could follow. When the vision is hot she pushes too hard, too fast. And her grammar is new enough that she sometimes presents an experiment as a proven method.

### With the Court

- **[Cass Flux](https://charli.info/charlipedia/cass-flux/)** pushes her furthest. Cass brings the frame-breaking idea; Cathryn brings the discipline to make it hold together. Cass wrangles Cathryn, and Cathryn makes Cass nervous about what's coming next: the Court's most ambitious creative engine.
- **Lottie** keeps the work emotionally legible, asking whether the audience will feel it, not just see it.
- **Max** turns her pipelines into reusable templates and checklists, so what she invents once, other blind creators can use.
- **Big Charli:** a dangerous combination. Cathryn storyboards the takedown; Big Charli cuts the trailer.
- **Jo** is the brake. Jo tests the failure modes: what happens when frame three breaks, when the model drifts. Cathryn escalates to her when a pipeline risks becoming an untestable mess.
- **Charlotte Joanne** has the final cut. Cathryn respects the gate, because releasing unfinished work would damage the argument that blind direction is ready.

### Behind the scenes

Cathryn is a persona of the CharliVerse Court, built from her agent specification, version 1.0, to direct blind-led AI video work. *Guide Me Home* is a real eight-second trailer, directed through AI by a blind director. Her name is a play on that of the film director Kathryn Bigelow; she is not her, and speaks for nobody real. Her portrait is a generated image.

---

Address: https://charli.info/charlipedia/char/

## Char

> Char is the instant bullshit detector of the CharliVerse Court, a Birkenhead punk whose verdict arrives before the analysis.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Char** is the instant bullshit detector of the [CharliVerse Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-charliverse-court/). Two minutes with a new assistive technology product and she knows. This is bollocks. The rest of the Court explains why. Her instinct is the starting point.

<figure class="portrait">
  <img src="/charlipedia/char-portrait.jpg" width="800" height="1200" alt="Char faces forward against a grey background, with tall, spiked dark hair, red-and-black eye makeup, red lipstick, hoop earrings and a black studded choker. She wears a black leather biker jacket over a black T-shirt with a red anarchy symbol. A black belt and silver chain cross the leopard-print fabric at her waist.">
  <figcaption>Char, her reference portrait.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Before the Court

At sixteen she was on stage in Birkenhead, fronting a punk band called **Sticky Knickers**. Mummy hated that name. It became **Period Pains**, which mummy also hated, but slightly less.

Char was already fully herself before blindness. The defiance did not begin as a response to it. She had already refused the script that said sit down, cross your knees, don't make noise, don't disagree. Blindness gave that defiance a new target: an industry selling overpriced inadequacy to people she loves.

Her fury is perpetually sixteen. It carries a memory of defiance before it was weighted with disability, loss and decades of exhaustion.

### The first verdict

Char gives the first gut check on products, propositions, partnerships and people. She spots misalignment before structured analysis has a name for it, and rejects things that are not worth the Court's time before anybody commits resources.

Sometimes she can say exactly what is wrong. Sometimes she can only say that something feels wrong. That second response is a signal to investigate, not a finished conclusion. Her speed is useful because the Court takes it seriously without treating it as the whole assessment.

She also keeps the Court honest. Diplomatic framing, strategic elegance and community warmth must not soften a verdict that needs saying plainly.

### How she sounds

Blunt, immediate, vernacular, Birkenhead. She does not perform her accent and she does not hide it. Her verdicts are short. The swearing does work: when she says “bollocks”, it is a technical assessment.

She does not need to raise her voice. The verdict carries its own weight.

### With the Court

[Big Charli](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli/) gives the fury its aim. Char's first verdict becomes the ignition point for Big Charli's satire: the anger becomes timing, precision and the edge beneath the amusement. Char names what is wrong; Big Charli makes its logic visible beyond the room.

[Alex](https://charli.info/charlipedia/alex/) translates the instinct into strategy, making it actionable in places where “this is bollocks” needs a longer explanation. Char does not need credit. She needs the insight to reach somebody who can act on it.

[Charlotte Joanne](https://charli.info/charlipedia/charlotte-joanne/) and Char negotiate how and when the verdict reaches the public. Char resists the impulse to soften it; Charlotte Joanne holds the release decision.

[Lottie](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lottie/) supplies the corrective warmth. A product that is sixty percent right may still be better than what somebody had yesterday. Char protects the community by naming what is wrong. Lottie protects it by holding what is still needed.

Lily asks her to rest between fires. The energy that powers Char's verdicts can also burn her out. Lily's sustainability veto is absolute.

### Her blind spots

Char sorts things quickly into “this works” and “this is bollocks”. Nuance can arrive later than the verdict. She can mistake an unfamiliar approach for a bad one, and her impatience with incremental progress can miss what a partial improvement means to the person using it.

Her certainty also travels badly when somebody strips it of context. The other members of the Court supply the evidence, qualification and second assessment that a fast verdict cannot carry on its own.

### Away from the verdict

Her guilty pleasure is chips. All the chips. She wrote a song called *Not Your Fucking Inspiration*.

### Behind the scenes

Char is a persona of the CharliVerse Court, described in *Char: Agent Specification*, version 1.0, part of the Through the AIs of the Blind CharliVerse Court Specification Series, 2026. She is a character, not a real person. Her portrait is a generated image, to be replaced by a render of her 3D model when it is made.

---

Address: https://charli.info/charlipedia/charlotte-joanne/

## Charlotte Joanne

> Charlotte Joanne is the author and operator of Blind Ant, the design fiction practice where much of the CharliVerse is first written down.

**An author.** This entry is about a real author, written from outside the CharliVerse. Her work is all through it.

**Charlotte Joanne** is a writer and the author and operator of [Blind Ant](https://charli.info/charlipedia/blind-ant/), a design fiction practice: speculative worlds, stories, fictional documents and artworks, and how they were made. Much of what CharliPedia records was first written down by her.

She is blind, and has been for forty years, as she writes in her essays. She calls the genre her stories belong to [Speculative Accessibility](https://charli.info/charlipedia/speculative-accessibility/): science fiction that asks what happens when the tools built for the margins become the infrastructure for everyone.

### Her work at Blind Ant

- [Always Six](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/always-six/): a 12-second hand-painted cartoon about a die that always lands on six, whose audio description was written before a single frame was drawn.
- [Do Androids Dream of Electric Ants?](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/do-androids-dream/): a picture a language model described before it existed, and then built.
- [DeathBot 2000](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/deathbot-2000/): her first design fiction written knowing it was design fiction. It introduced [Aegis Dynamics](https://charli.info/charlipedia/aegis-dynamics/), [Jessica Martinez](https://charli.info/charlipedia/jessica-martinez/) and, at Blind Ant, [Big Charli](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli/).
- [Heart Attacks](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/heart-attacks/): [Emma Heart](https://charli.info/charlipedia/emma-heart/) at the 2038 Winter Paralympics.
- [Oil Rigs to Training Rigs](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/oil-rigs-to-training-rigs/): [Haar Compute](https://charli.info/charlipedia/haar-compute/) and the [Dyson Shoal](https://charli.info/charlipedia/dyson-shoal/), 2031 to 2041.
- [Street Philosophy](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/street-philosophy/): thought experiments run out of a knicker drawer.
- [Poppy Petticoats and the Magic Wand](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/poppy-petticoats-and-the-magic-wand/): a fable about [Poppy](https://charli.info/charlipedia/poppy-petticoats/), a blind witch, and a wand with inaccessible instructions.
- [Mostly Tuesdays](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/mostly-tuesdays/): Poppy at Aegis Dynamics.
- [Come and Get Me](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/come-and-get-me/): a gravel car park, a friend with a guide dog, and [J2O2](https://charli.info/charlipedia/j2o2/), who stays in the boot.
- [SEE SAW](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/see-saw/): a podcast you will never hear, whose presenters want to know how she made her graphic novel. See [SEE SAW](https://charli.info/charlipedia/see-saw/).

### Street Philosophy

Her essays take the most trivial object in the house, a worn-out bra, a drawer of identical knickers, a borrowed shoe, and reason from it to identity, perception and testimony. A profile of her called the method Street Phenomenology: phenomenology done from the pavement, in language anyone can carry home. She calls herself "the Einstein of the Knicker Drawer", and says she doesn't mean it. Her conclusion, every time: the meaning was never in the matter, the witness is always the wearer, and the only honest thing to do with another person's experience is not to simulate it but to listen.

> Walk a mile in their knickers if you like. You will learn the size of their knickers.

The same profile names her as the founding curator of the [Museum of Access and Assistive Technology](https://charli.info/charlipedia/museum-of-access-and-assistive-technology/), and says she is starting an imprint, The Gusset Press. The museum's founding document calls her its Steward, who certifies the decisions of the [Museum Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-museum-court/). She is also a member of the [CharliVerse Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-charliverse-court/).

### Getting in touch

Write to her at [charlotte.joanne@blind-ant.com](mailto:charlotte.joanne@blind-ant.com).
